items.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: we found something called “I’d Give a Dollar for a Dime” with lyrics by Andy Razaf.

ctx.x: Do you have any stories that you could tell us about perhaps some gigs you’ve done with Joe Williams?

Well, Joe, first of all I think that Joe is the greatest jazz singer there ever was. And I think his sense of time is just about as good as any great drummer in the business. And the funny thing was that one of the things that I did with Joe I didn’t play on at all, but we were doing a show in tribute to Eubie Blake called “Eubie’s Hundred Years” or something like that. It was on the occasion of his hundredth birthday. It was a show on public television out of Washington. Joe was one of the guests and part of the…
